DNA storage provides a durable and long-term storage solution for digital data. While previous research has focused on efficient methods for encoding and decoding binary data using DNA, there has been less attention given to managing hierarchical digital data effectively. This paper addresses this gap by introducing a new DNA storage system that effectively supports the encoding of data hierarchies and efficient update functionality. Unlike existing encoders that treat input data as flat binary, our system encodes data in a format that maintains its original hierarchical structure, thereby simplifying updates and reducing the amount of DNA required. Experimental evaluations show that our system outperforms a flat-encoding approach in terms of storage usage and updatability, and offers particular advantages for data with complex hierarchies.

Precise and efficient river flow velocity predictions are crucial for various applications such as managing flood risks. While the shallow water equations are commonly employed for this purpose, traditional numerical solutions struggle with speed and are often too cumbersome for real-time use. In contrast, the proposed NeuralRiver model leverages neural networks to solve the shallow water equations quickly and efficiently. By combining a unique combination of neural network-based solutions to the continuous and discrete shallow water equations, NeuralRiver delivers precise and rapid flow velocity predictions. The model's effectiveness is demonstrated through successful river flow velocity predictions using the Loughborough 2D flume dataset, outperforming established traditional numerical methods. Additionally, NeuralRiver exhibits significant speedup over these methods, showcasing its potential for real-time river flow velocity predictions in various settings.

HDR photography combines multiple photos captured at various exposure levels to counterbalance digital cameras' limited dynamic range. This research presents a novel technique for automatically determining the optimal exposure settings for HDR image creation using smartphone cameras. A sample dataset consisting of 500 images was used to establish optimal exposure levels, which were found to be at their brightest and middle exposures. A fusion algorithm based on HDR techniques was also developed to create HDR images from multiple photos captured at distinct exposure levels. The research evaluated multiple metrics for assessing the quality of HDR images generated using this method. Results showed that the proposed technique outperformed existing methods in terms of visual appeal and metric scores.

Causal deep learning is a recent approach that aims to integrate causal knowledge into deep learning models, enabling them to make more accurate predictions and inferences. This field, which has gained significant momentum in recent years, employs methods that directly utilize causal information and have been demonstrated through various studies to surpass the performance of conventional deep learning techniques. Nevertheless, existing research primarily focuses on supervised learning and does not adequately address important unsupervised and semi-supervised learning problems. Furthermore, there is a lack of clear guidelines for evaluating and selecting causal deep learning methods. In an attempt to address these limitations and expand the scope of causal deep learning to include both structured and unstructured data, this paper introduces a new category it dubs "high-density learning." High-density learning refers to learning from densely interconnected and complex data systems characterized by multiple interconnected components and interconnections. Or, alternatively, it can mean learning from densely packed and highly representative data sets that contain substantial amounts of valuable information. This paper explores both interpretations of high-density learning and presents a novel technique called Structural Attention Network (SAN) that is capable of handling both dense internal structures and dense data features. Through thorough experiments conducted on multiple challenging problems, the efficacy of SAN is clearly demonstrated, especially when compared to more conventional methods.

This note presents a new category of map functions known as oriented link map functions, which incorporates both structured map functions and a new concept that can be understood as a variation of the classical Nash inequality, often referred to as the Conley index. Building on the work of Figalli and others, we demonstrate that highly regular oriented link map functions belong to a specific polynomial class, a result that implies the Mumford Conjecture.

Understanding the behavior of multilevel preconditioners for solving balance equations in biomechanics is crucial for optimizing computation time and memory usage. This investigation compares the performance of two multilevel preconditioning methods, ALBERT and 1D-ELASTIC, employing synthetic and real-world data from cardiac mechanics simulations. Different memory usage and computation time results are presented, demonstrating how changing key parameters affects the methods' performance. Generally, ALBERT exhibits better computation time results but higher memory usage, whereas 1D-ELASTIC shows better memory usage but longer computation times. Ultimately, this study highlights the significance of experimenting with various parameters to balance memory usage and computation time for real-world applications.

Standard diffusion models can fail, particularly when influenced by correlations and variations, where mean squared displacements grow in a linear manner with time. We investigate the spread of a fractional Brownian population exhibiting time-dependent and diverse diffusion characteristics. Our primary objective is to establish the relationship between these individual characteristics and the population's spatial distribution as observed over time. We examine the applicability and limitations of this approach to a broad category of self-similar diffusion processes, utilizing a general framework that is subsequently applied to recognized processes such as Laplace diffusion, nonlinear diffusion, and their variants.

A fundamental theory is developed to describe both linear and Kerr nonlinear interactions between the modes of dielectric optical resonators, with the framework being applicable across various geometries and modes. The general approach allows for a wide range of phenomena resulting from linear interactions, scattering, and Kerr nonlinearity, such as mode coupling and phase modulation, to be analyzed. The developed theory is specifically applied to a waveguide with a microresonator in close proximity, enabling the computation of mode coupling and phase modulation terms. Furthermore, a dimensionless equation is derived to describe the dynamics of two identical counterpropagating modes in a loop resonator and, under the condition of mode identity, it is proven that cross-phase modulation is precisely twice as strong as self-phase modulation.

A novel high-resolution model is proposed to reconstruct turbulent flow dynamics in a specific range of Reynolds numbers from low-resolution data. The proposed framework, comprising two main components, allows for precise reconstruction of high-resolution velocity patterns. Initially, a standard convolutional neural network generates an estimate of high-resolution velocity based on low-resolution input. To refine this prediction, another separately trained model using the estimate and low-resolution input produces an improved outcome. The proposed framework achieves superior results for turbulent flow reconstruction compared to a single-stage prediction approach and accurately simulates turbulent flow characteristics, including non-linear instability and random pattern formation. Furthermore, the proposed method demonstrates reasonable accuracy in predicting realistic turbulence patterns and modelled flow characteristics in a separated Reynolds number range.

Despite notable breakthroughs in reinforcement learning, numerous significant hurdles remain when applying it to dynamic and ever-changing problems common in critical domains, including robotics and complex gameplay. Reinforcement learning models generally struggle to generalize effectively when confronted with new tasks beyond their training data. In response to this challenge, the field is seeing an increased focus on continual learning methods, and to support this research, new tools are being developed, including carefully crafted evaluation frameworks and benchmark environments. To address this need, we present Lifelong Learning Explorer (L2Explorer), a cutting-edge Unity-based environment that allows for continuous, flexible experimentation in a 3D, immersive exploration setting. L2Explorer is distinct from procedurally generated worlds, which often incorporate randomized components. Instead, we've developed a structured and systematic approach to creating learning curricula in response to controlled changes, along with complementary metrics to assess transfer, performance, and data efficiency. The comprehensive framework and methodology we've established with L2Explorer provide a crucial platform for advancing future evaluation methods and rigorous assessment of lifelong learning strategies.

Understanding business processes relies heavily on knowing what processes are in place, rather than the details of how they function. As a result, there is growing interest in declaring processes using logic-based representations, which can be easily shared and examined by various stakeholders. Although there are established methods for detecting and investigating imperative processes, they are less applicable to declarative processes due to these processes' distinct characteristics. In response to this need, we have developed a protocol to monitor and investigate declarative processes in real-time, even with incomplete information, using a logic program that incorporates input streams. Additionally, we have integrated a variety of inquiry techniques that enable efficient queries about the processes being examined, even in the presence of uncertainty, by utilizing constraint propagation and sorting. Our approach and associated protocol have been demonstrated through experimental usage on real-world datasets.

This informal note aims to supplement the rigorous proof provided in Reference [1], particularly the algebraic proof presented in Section 2.2. We begin by illustrating how the geometric interpretation of local algebraic completeness can be naturally incorporated into the moduli space of curves, specifically within the context of genus one surfaces and separating divisors. We then go on to consider non-singular Deligne-Mumford curves of genus one with one branch point, examining the extension of the moduli space in both the classical sense and the algebraic sense. We show that in this scenario, the algebraic extension is equivalent to the non-sensical case of defining the genus through the Chern class of a symmetric tensor. We also discuss the relationship between the two extensions in a more general context, focusing on when the algebraic extension is both larger and smaller than the geometric extension.

Determining the factors behind the decline of the mass-star formation rate proportionality in massive galaxies has been analyzed through a a three-component model: incorporating light-free, star-forming, and quiescent galaxy populations. A prior study found that removing quiescent galaxies does not explain the proportionality's decline, whereas removing light-free galaxies does. This paper investigates whether this result holds when considering the contributions of active galactic nuclei (AGNs). By utilizing a wide range of data, including optical, infrared, X-ray, and radio observations, our research finds that the proportionality's decline is evident across all galaxy luminosity ranges and that the contribution of AGNs to star formation is generally small, except in the high-luminosity range. Nonetheless, the diminishment of the proportionality remains when removing light-free galaxies. If we focus on an all-wave range, the result persists; but, if we consider infrared data alone, the result disappears. This distinction may be attributed to the influence of AGNs on the infrared measurement of star formation, which can be disentangled using a threshold based on nuclear luminosity. Above a certain threshold, the proportionality begins to decline. Therefore, the role of AGNs, especially in infrared measurements, is crucial for interpreting the mass-star formation rate proportionality.

This paper conducts a sentiment analysis across languages, examining the
emotional content of news articles using both positive and negative sentiment
categories. The primary motivation is to provide a linguistic-agnostic method
to gauge the overall psychological atmosphere of a given language, as
indicated by the analysis. The research focuses on English, Spanish, and
Portuguese but can be applied to other languages with similar grammatical
structures. The proposed multi-task, minority-class approach addresses issues
related to extreme imbalanced data, incorporating a sampling technique and
asymmetric loss functions to achieve improved performance. The evaluation shows
significant gains in model performance for smaller language classes, and the
psychological atmosphere represented by the generated embeddings aligns with
human assessments.

X-ray images contain subtle characteristics that can predict patients' critical health status.  If accurately identified, these features hold significant promise in directing limited intensive care unit resources to the most needy patients.  Through the analysis of 162 COVID-19 patient X-ray images, our research demonstrated the use of statistical methods to extract relevant attributes from the images.  These attributes were then utilized in machine learning-based approaches to classify patients as either severe or mild cases based on their current condition.  Our results showed that even without accounting for patient history, we could effectively identify severe cases with an accuracy of over 90%.  By incorporating clinical data, our models achieved near perfect accuracy.  Our study provides a foundation for further exploration into using artificial intelligence to extract valuable information from X-ray images, as well as incorporating patient history and other clinical information.

The universal simplicial collection (UTC) is a highly versatile construct that arises from the principle that the natural transformation associated with a given object and valuing in a Yoneda style embedding is universal in terms of consistency under the functor that converts collections into commutative algebras, up to natural isomorphism. Building upon this foundation, we demonstrate that the UTC is inherently a simplicial group by connecting it to the fundamental group in the context of higher category theory. This association allows us to redefine the UTC as the result of applying the free group functor to the fundamental group, thereby establishing that the UTC is, in fact, a free simplicial group.

This paper delves into the source of a significant error category in Visual Relationship Detection (VRD), namely the incorrect association of relationships between objects within images. We argue that existing models fail to achieve high precision due to an uneven class balance problem caused by valuable 'positive' classes being overwhelmed by numerous harmful 'positive' instances. To address this, we propose a novel class-aware approach, dividing VRD tasks into three distinct categories: a majority 'background' consisting of unwanted relationships, a middle ground 'ambivalent' encompassing difficult-to-distinguish classes, and a minimal 'foreground' of clear relationships. By customizing the annotation as training data, our method demonstrates significant precision improvements on existing benchmarks while equally matching their recall performance.

We've performed an in-depth analysis of three galaxy cores at $\rm z=2.91$ within a massive galaxy group, yielding high-resolution infrared and submillimeter data. This revealed that the galaxies exhibit extremely compact, actively star-forming cores at the centers of massive, irregularly shaped disk systems, both of which exhibit quiescent, lopsided characteristics. Consequently, these galaxies are witnessing `outside-in' quenching. We propose a theoretical framework suggesting that mass asymmetry, resulting from absorbed and irregular matter, is accountable for their diminished star-formation activity by channeling it towards their core. Furthermore, we observe that disk asymmetry is associated with gas streams that are feeding the galaxies and influencing their evolution. This is manifested by an aligned major-axis of galaxies in relation to nearby filaments, presenting observational evidence of accretion streams on galaxy evolution. This is demonstrated by bulge construction, combined with massive quiescent, lopsided galaxies in the current stage, until they collide with a major merger galaxy.

Recently discovered solar neutron decay particles, which were detected on November 7, 2004, during a significant solar flare, have sparked fascinating insights into neutron star physics. Essentially unseen in previous solar observations, this new phenomenon has researchers re-examining data from GCR collisions with protons. By re-analyzing these events, scientists have identified a distinctive pattern of GCR neutrons colliding with atmospheric nitrogen, thereby transforming into unstable delta-isobars, which then decay into protons. This discovery has significant implications for the study of neutron stars, particularly in regards to their strange matter composition, and it also sheds light on the stability of delta-isobars. Moreover, this finding has tangible applications in forecasting solar neutron decay events and understanding the effects of strange quarks on neutron star physics.

This study reveals intriguing evidence of rapid spin acceleration in low-mass stars, including one that is departing from equilibrium, as observed in G-K type stars. Utilizing spectroscopic data from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey, we determined the rotation rates for 1.5 to 5 solar mass stars and investigated their relationship with stellar parameters. Our analysis shows that younger low-mass stars are more likely to exhibit high rotation rates, indicating the preservation of initial angular momentum. This finding is consistent with recent findings by Tan et al. (2014). However, unlike Tan et al., we noticed a distinct group of younger low-mass stars that are spinning at extremely high rates, likely due to angular momentum accumulation through planetary incorporation or an unknown internal mechanism.

TruthSeeker: a dataset of 1.5 million articles with 12 million text and 240 thousand image features, spanning false news stories that have emerged in the past and others that have not, is utilized to introduce a system for falsely verifying news. This system, consisting of three components, first generates a base model tailored to the specific news format it is designing for, whether text-based or image-based, using a neural process method. This base model is then applied in a way that is both efficient and effective to score the likelihood of falsely verifying each news item, with the option of incorporating the reader's subjective probability of believing the news. Experimental findings indicate that this system yields superior results than alternative methods, demonstrating significant gains in AUC scores of 6% and 12% for text-based and image-based false news detection, respectively.

This research paper examines a novel transport equation featuring an non-local term and cyclic behavior. Cyclic patterns occur when a function changes over time in a specific way, reflecting the behavior of a system through which a substance is transported and mixed within a bounded space. We have derived inequalities that help identify the structure of which solutions are part, and in turn, this structure is utilized to demonstrate the existence of solutions near particular singularity types. Complicated situations are addressed by combining our equations with systems of the Navier-Stokes type.

Recently, Golay complementary sequences have gained popularity due to their utility in omnidirectional code construction. This research extends Golay complementary sequences to higher-dimensional spaces by developing a concept called multi-dimensional Golay complementary arrays. A new classification of two-dimensional Golay complementary arrays is introduced, incorporating a parameter that represents the period of the arrays in one dimension. It is demonstrated that all one-dimensional Golay complementary arrays participate in this category. The paper also explores large sets of multi-dimensional Golay complementary arrays that can be utilized in omnidirectional codes. A specific example of a two-dimensional Golay complementary array with an extended period is provided, along with its generating matrices. This example comprises four different one-dimensional Golay complementary arrays, each with a distinct period.

Quantum tunneling is an inherent process that lacks a direct analogy in classical physics, and it can rival Coulomb interactions to give rise to intricate phenomena.
In silicon, precise placement of phosphorus dopants is feasible to address the diverse consequences of this interplay, however this approach depends on wave functions related to crystal symmetry, which quantum tunneling inherently affects.
In this study, lattice-aperiodic valley interference patterns were directly visualized in silicon by employing scanning tunneling microscopy to investigate coupled atoms.
The examination reveals the significance of envelope anisotropy, valley interference and the location of the dopants on Heisenberg's spin swapping, which occurs in silicon.
In turn, this indicates that envelope anisotropy and valley interference are crucial factors in controlling the interplay between Coulomb and Coulomb-like interactions in silicon, and the unique properties related to them hold value in quantum computing and solid-state quantum optics.

Complex systems consisting of multiple interacting components typically follow nonlinear dynamics that are difficult to predict using traditional methods. Neural network-based models, while effective for short-term predictions, can struggle with scalability and failing to account for the underlying framework of the system. In contrast, graph neural networks offer a more lasting way to capture dynamics and topology equally, without needing extensive training. Our advisory framework encourages the equal learning importance of topology over dynamics, leading to a 10% improvement in long-term prediction accuracy. When advised to prioritize dynamics, it successfully reveals nonlinear relationships and complex interactions, confirming the efficacy of graph neural networks. Our code is available at https://github.com/wenhong1999/CxGNP.

We introduce an infinite sequence of recursive formulas for calculating the number of distinct partitions of natural numbers, drawing on concepts from homotopy theory and modular forms. These formulas, inspired by the division properties of modular forms, emerge from the interplay between polynomial divisions and the construction of certain objects in homotopy theory, specifically through a process called functorial generation. A specific formula involving the Euler phi-function, Catalan numbers, and 24-digit integer combinations arises from analyzing a particular set of partitions under the modular group Σ24. Moreover, our investigation leads to the discovery of recursive formulas for well-known number sequences, including the number of polyominoes, alternating permutations, and structure functions of composite numbers.

A head injury's severity can be determined by the extent and type of brain damage, which requires in-depth knowledge of brain anatomy. However, determining this severity is complicated by the various perspectives that can be used, including 2D facial views, 3D reconstructed images, and clinical information. A joint model is proposed that simultaneously processes multiple perspectives to create a severity level. The model consists of two main components: a joint variational auto-encoder (VAE) and a discriminator. The VAE processes facial images and reconstructed 3D brain images to create a severity level. The discriminator ensures that the VAE's encoded severity level accurately reflects the input images' characteristics. As images from different viewpoints have significant differences in features, a novel progressive 2D VAE is introduced to handle facial images. This model successively adds latent variables at different layers to achieve better feature representation, resulting in improved performance compared to traditional VAE methods. The proposed algorithm is applied to mock image generation representing diffuse axonal injury, demonstrating its effectiveness.

GP 2 is a graph-based language designed for efficient program analysis and verification, leveraging graph transformation rules to ease these tasks. However, efficiently developing GP 2 programs poses difficulties, primarily stemming from the time-consuming nature of graph matching. To overcome this limitation, the GP 2 framework incorporates a type of rooted rule that can be matched rapidly, given certain conditions are met. In order to accelerate the GP 2 compiler, several key modifications have been made to Bak's compiler, including a data structure optimisation for dynamic arrays known as BigArray. This novel structure, characterised by successive size increments of its components, enhances compiler performance. As evidence of the compiler's speed-enhancing benefits, a case study is presented showcasing the GP 2 compiler's application in optimising the runtime efficiency of a program aimed at detecting binary DAGs. This previously time-consuming operation is now executed at a linear rate following the compiler upgrade.

In recent years, contrastive learning has gained significant attention in the feature extraction domain due to its ability to draw on comparable pairs to train effective models. To enhance performance, many methods have been developed with sophisticated architecture designs, such as using multiple projection layers. However, these approaches often divide contrastive learning tasks into multiple stages without considering unified structures. In response to this observation, a new unified structure for feature extraction through contrastive learning has been proposed, incorporating multiple stages into a single, compact framework. Theoretical and experimental evidence demonstrates that this structure yields optimal results, surpassing the performance of multi-stage methods and rivaling state-of-the-art results in various feature extraction tasks.

We have established that the star normal quotient property holds for the locally arc-transitive graphs obtained from a graph $\Gamma$ by applying a composition operation, where $\Gamma$ possesses certain symmetry properties and includes a vertex-transitive covering. This covering is specified by a set of covering mappings that map $\Gamma$ to itself and satisfy specific compatibility conditions. Moreover, this category includes graph automorphisms derived from the automorphisms of the covering, which form a subgroup of the covering's automorphism group. Notably, one key example within this category is provided by the twisted wreath construction. To that end, we define the twisted wreath graph $\Gamma_{tw}(G,r)$ as resulting from the composition operation applied to a vertex-transitive covering, under certain specified criteria. We then determine the structural characteristics of this graph, including its component graphs, and identify its automorphism group.

Working with categorical data for model selection and sparse modeling becomes increasingly complex as the number of variables grows, as it typically requires a parameter for each category, making interpretation challenging. Despite its efficiency for handling continuous and categorical variables, the Group Lasso often results in inconsistent estimates, rendering the model difficult to interpret due to the lack of sparsity. To achieve a sparse solution using the Group Lasso, we propose a two-step method: first reducing data dimensions through the Group Lasso, and then employing an information criterion on a subset of clustered models. This algorithm's performance is evaluated under high-dimensional conditions and compared with state-of-the-art methods using synthetic and real-world datasets, showing its superior performance in terms of prediction accuracy and model size.

Recent advances in large language models have achieved human-like performance on numerous language tasks. However, the potential for these models to effectively utilize structured information, particularly within knowledge graphs, compared to free-form text, has not been extensively explored. To bridge this knowledge gap, our approach develops a method to integrate structured knowledge into LLMs through training on specific knowledge graph triples. We demonstrate that LLMs pre-trained with our technique on a vast knowledge base like Wikidata outperform conventional T5 models in various evaluation benchmarks. Specifically, our approach shows comparable performance when compared to training models on descriptive language containing the same information, and significantly improves performance when utilizing smaller knowledge graphs. One key advantage of this method is the absence of a requirement to synchronize knowledge graphs with text data, making it highly suitable for large-scale knowledge graphs.

Achieving a seamless visual experience and optimal system performance when displaying line joins on vector maps requires an efficient anti-aliasing technique. However, the limitations of OpenGL API hinder optimal rendering results when approximating the anti-aliased effect through multiple triangles. In an attempt to rectify this issue, this study introduces a straightforward yet high-performance algorithm utilizing two triangles to replicate fan-shaped line joins via alpha operation. Our findings indicate this technique yields a genuine anti-aliasing effect while reducing memory consumption, raising frame rates, and preventing overlap rendering in map visualization. Our novel anti-aliasing method has been applied in notable applications such as Tencent Mobile Maps and Tencent Automotive Maps.

To effectively capture sequential patterns in noisy audio, a new Dual-Path Convolution Recurrent Network has been proposed, combining the strengths of both convolutional and recurrent structures. By dividing the model into two distinct pathways, one for immediate clean signal features and the other for noisy signal training, a joint loss function can be employed to integrate the features. This results in a model that is both efficient and capable of capturing long-term dependencies, leading to a significant improvement in speech enhancement performance. Evaluations conducted on the intense noise conditions of the IEEE-ASPA 2020 challenge and the various environment conditions of the MIRCOSITE dataset demonstrate the efficacy of this model, with DPCRN outperforming existing methods by considerable margins of 10.11% and 12.13% in the STOI metric, respectively.

Recently introduced multi-fluid models hold promise in refining the simulation of atmospheric convection within weather and climate simulations. A dynamic framework by nature, this method eliminates several of the mass-flux convection scheme's assumptions that are no longer valid at modern model resolution levels. Nonetheless, the optimal approach for solving the multi-fluid equations in relation to atmospheric convection remains unknown. The present paper outlines a simple single-column two-fluid model featuring ascending and descending fluid components with the exclusion of additional sub-filter variation modelling. Subsequent application to Rayleigh-Benard convection yields encouraging results as even a rudimentary model successfully replicates the prevalent characteristic overturning patterns of convection over a wide range of driving forces, accurately estimating the associated heat transfer scaling across six orders of magnitude.

We investigate three separate Jaynes-Cummings systems, with two of the systems having correlated atoms, while the third system is unconnected. Our goal is to determine when this unconnected system can be entangled with the other two, despite initially being uncorrelated. This will depend on the systems' parameters, specifically how they relate to the resonance frequency and its deviation. Our analysis shows that a specific condition must be met to create entanglement between the unconnected system and the others. Below a certain threshold of entanglement, we can provide a precise bound on the unconnected system's entanglement. Additionally, we examine two of the Jaynes-Cummings systems merging into one, with the unconnected system remaining separate. This occurs when the frequency deviation is significant enough that the two systems operate outside of each other's resonance range. We can also determine the probability of this outcome.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
organizations and individuals to track the public's emotions towards them and their rivals.
As a result, analyzing public sentiment has become both crucial and difficult to accomplish.
In this project, we gathered and manually annotated seven freely accessible Twitter sentiment
databases. We then compiled an LSTM-based model to classify the stated sentiments. The model's
performance was assessed using the newly acquired data, along with results from established
benchmarks. The findings are as follows: we optimized an LSTM-based model that surpasses the
performance of other widely used methods on three of the seven datasets, demonstrates
comparable performance on three more, and fails to improve the other dataset; the model's
performance on all seven datasets is equivalent when using a different optimizer, demonstrating
no difference when using ten different hyperparameter settings on two of the seven
datasets, a significant difference on three more, and no notable effect on the other two.

Power law non-linear electrodynamics features a non-linear interaction between electric and thermal fields. We investigate the dynamics of black holes in power law non-linear electrodynamics under both local and global thermodynamic equilibrium within a shaded background. Local thermodynamic stability analysis indicates that the heat capacity becomes positive at a certain temperature, thereby preventing the system from generating an infinite amount of energy through the combination of electromagnetic and thermal energy. Furthermore, we discovered that the temperature of the system transitions from an adiabatic phase transition to an abrupt shift as the non-linear parameter increases. Moreover, we found that the temperature of the system increases under global thermodynamic non-equilibrium conditions with the accumulation of accumulated energy. We also examined the relationship between the emitted electromagnetic radiation and the shade depth. Our results indicate that the shape of the temperature curve changes depending on the non-linear parameter, with $\alpha > 1$ exhibiting a more complex behavior than $\alpha < 1$. Additionally, we found that the heat capacity becomes positive at a certain temperature, thereby preventing the system from generating an infinite amount of energy through the combination of electromagnetic and thermal energy. Furthermore, we found that the temperature of the system increases under global thermodynamic non-equilibrium conditions with the accumulation of accumulated energy.
